0.notes: D-dominant: regulatory rights and catchment management impose strong constraints. Single actor (PUB) eliminates inter-institutional coordination costs at this boundary.
0.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

1.notes: High PUB transparency; abstraction data published in Annual Reports. No third-party verification of intake meters.
1.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

2.notes: Highest transparency phase: statutory monitoring, external quality audits. Sub-process Event 4 (preliminary screening) is internal.
2.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

3.notes: Closed infrastructure; no third-party access. Opacity at this phase is structural (physical inaccessibility), not institutional.
3.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

4.notes: Per-capita consumption is the most publicly cited metric. Leakage <4.5% (PUB 2023) — among lowest globally.
4.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

5.notes: PUB operates Deep Tunnel Sewerage System — unified, modern collection infrastructure. High system integrity; minimal inflow/infiltration. Contrast with OCWD where OC San collection system is older and partially self-reported.
5.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

6.notes: PUB operates all WRPs directly. No institutional handoff at this boundary. Contrast: OCWD's OC San operates primary/secondary; OCWD operates advanced treatment — boundary crossing here.
6.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

7.notes: All PUB-operated. Minimum boundary score (2) reflects genuine structural distinction between biological and advanced chemical treatment, confirmed by measurable quality output.
7.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

8.notes: ZERO inter-institutional handoff. PUB receives its own secondary effluent and applies advanced treatment within the same organisational boundary. This is the phase where multi-actor water-reuse systems can incur inter-agency handoff cost. Energy: ~3.5 kWh/m³ (MF+RO+UV; PUB Annual Report).
8.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

9.notes: Highest transparency: externally verified quality data published monthly and annually. Certification gives NEWater its legal status for indirect potable reuse (reservoir blending).
9.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

10.notes: PUB controls dedicated purple-pipe distribution network directly. No handoff to third-party distributors. Contrast: OCWD distributes to Irvine Ranch Water District, Mesa Water, and other municipal agencies — each is a separate institutional boundary.
10.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input

11.notes: Loop closure: PUB controls both the contributing end (NEWater distribution) and the receiving end (PUB reservoirs). The tholonic recursion is structurally intact — Phase 11 child-N becomes Phase 0 parent-N through a single actor. This is the fundamental structural advantage over multi-actor groundwater-reuse systems, where loop closure can pass through a shared groundwater commons.
11.scope_source: Not provided — requires separate data input
